question: An engineer is implementing FCoE. Which aspect of DCBXP on a Cisco Nexus switch affects this implementation?
options: It requires that LLDP transmit and LLDP receive are enabled on the FCoE interface.
It uses the Cisco Fabric Services protocol to exchange parameters between two peer links.
It provides the authentication of peers on the Cisco Nexus switch.
It always is enabled on 10/100-Mbps native Ethernet ports.
theory: Data Center Bridging Exchange Protocol (DCBXP) is an extension of LLDP that Cisco Nexus switches use to negotiate PFC, ETS, and other lossless-Ethernet parameters with a CNA before FCoE traffic can flow. Because DCBXP TLVs ride inside LLDP frames, LLDP transmit and receive must both be enabled on the FCoE-facing interface for DCBXP - and therefore FCoE - to operate; if either direction of LLDP is disabled, capability negotiation with the adapter fails. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 9 - Data Center Bridging Exchange (DCBX))
